primary_source.title: Government of Georgia Decree No. 447 of 15 September 2026 — Rule for Planning and Implementing Water Resource Monitoring

verified_main_text_claims.claim: The National Environmental Agency prepares the annual state water-resource monitoring plan and submits it to the Minister for approval no later than 1 December each year.
Monitoring data are to be retained in standardized formats; access is provided subject to environmental-information, data-protection and confidentiality law.
The state monitoring plan must be representative, risk-based and use standardized methods and indices to support comparability over time.
The rule distinguishes observational, operational and investigative monitoring; operational monitoring applies to at-risk water bodies and is described as monthly or quarterly.

secondary_source.title: Government Decree No. 447/2026 — reproduced text and annex transcription
inspected_sections: Annex 2, Table 3 — groundwater monitoring methods and equipment
secondary_source.limitation: The page identifies Matsne as the official source, but this transcription has not been independently compared byte-for-byte with the official DOCX attachment.

groundwater_sampling_method_transcriptio.pumped_wells: Use low-flow sampling where pumping rate can be controlled to minimize disturbance and obtain a representative sample.
groundwater_sampling_method_transcriptio.artesian_wells_and_springs: Choose a method consistent with natural-flow conditions and representative-sample requirements.
groundwater_sampling_method_transcriptio.objective: Minimize changes in the sample's physical and chemical characteristics.

interpretation_limits: The official Matsne HTML main text was inspected, but its listed 46,049-byte DOCX annex was not retrieved, parsed or hashed.
All Annex-specific frequencies and sampling-method details in this record are secondary transcription leads, not independently verified primary-source facts.
Do not operationalize Annex-specific frequencies until the official DOCX is obtained, hashed and compared with the transcription.
State environmental water-resource monitoring is distinct from drinking-water supplier compliance sampling under the separate potable-water legal regime.

The 1 December deadline is a duty to submit the annual state water-resource monitoring plan for ministerial approval; it is not evidence that the plan was submitted, approved, published or implemented.
No sample-level measurements, station identifiers, coordinates, personal data or restricted annex bytes are included.
